1.mascotDialogue: extract-max is really two moves — swap the root with the last leaf, shrink the heap by one, then let that displaced value sink on down to wherever it truly belongs.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 4 and 5 find the biggest of the node and its two children. Line 8's recursive call is what lets that displaced value keep sinkin' past more'n one level if it's gotta.

3.mascotDialogue: 9's sittin' right up top, and every parent down this tree beats out both its kids — same array-index math as min heap, just the comparison flipped clean around.

4.mascotDialogue: That swap alone don't finish the job. Without siftDown, you've just moved the problem up to the top of the tree instead of actually fixin' it.
